arguments.command: read -p "🔌 Port to free: " port && pid=$(lsof -ti :"$port") && tput cuu 1 && if [ -n "$pid" ]; then termy_say "Freeing port $port" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "\r\n" && kill -9 $pid && echo -e "✅ Killed process $pid on port \033[1m$port\033[22m"; else termy_say "No process found on port $port" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "\r\nNo process found on port $port"; fi && printf ""
arguments.explanation: Prompts for a port number, identifies the listening process PID using lsof, and terminates it using kill -9.
arguments.goal: Terminate the process listening on a specific port

arguments.command: read -p "⌨️  Command to watch: " cmd && tput cuu 1 && termy_say "Monitoring command" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "\r\n" && watch -n 2 "$cmd" && printf ""
arguments.explanation: Prompts the user for a command and uses the watch utility to run it repeatedly every 2 seconds.
arguments.goal: Monitor a command output in real time

arguments.command: tput cuu 1 && termy_say "Displaying PATH entries" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "\r\n" && echo "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' && printf ""
arguments.explanation: Splits the PATH environment variable by colons and prints each directory on a new line.
arguments.goal: List PATH directories line by line
